info.name: Digilux OTA API v1.8
info.description:
REST API collection for the Digilux Over-The-Air (OTA) update system.

**Base URL:** `https://iot.digilux.co.in/smarthome`

---

## Auth Tokens

**Admin token** (for Packages, Deployments, Device folders):
```
aws cognito-idp initiate-auth \
  --auth-flow USER_PASSWORD_AUTH \
  --client-id q7189jitfkk4ttesepkgls491 \
  --auth-parameters USERNAME=mahesh.maney@gmail.com,PASSWORD=Admin@1234 \
  --region ap-south-1 \
  --query 'AuthenticationResult.IdToken' \
  --output text
```
Paste into the `admin_token` collection variable.

**User token** (for End User Updates folder):
```
aws cognito-idp initiate-auth \
  --auth-flow USER_PASSWORD_AUTH \
  --client-id q7189jitfkk4ttesepkgls491 \
  --auth-parameters USERNAME=demotesthw5@yopmail.com,PASSWORD=DigiluxOTA@Test1 \
  --region ap-south-1 \
  --query 'AuthenticationResult.IdToken' \
  --output text
```
Paste into the `user_token` collection variable.

---

## Folder Structure

| Folder | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| Packages | `admin_token` | Upload & manage firmware packages |
| Device (Admin) | `admin_token` | Admin device update check |
| Deployments | `admin_token` | Create & manage fleet deployments |
| Full Deployment Flow | `admin_token` | End-to-end admin upload → deploy sequence |
| End User Updates | `user_token` | User-initiated update flow (Flutter app) |

---

## Collection Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `base_url` | API base URL |
| `admin_token` | Cognito ID token — admin group user |
| `user_token` | Cognito ID token — regular user (owns test device) |
| `device_id` | Test device UUID |
| `job_id` | Auto-populated by Create Deployment / Give Consent |
| `consent_id` | Auto-populated by Give Consent |
| `upload_url` | Auto-populated by Get Upload URL (SINGLE mode) |
| `upload_id` | Auto-populated by Get Upload URL (MULTIPART mode) |
| `upload_type` | `SINGLE` or `MULTIPART` — set by Get Upload URL |
| `package_name` | Package name for requests |
| `package_version` | Package version for requests |

item.name: Packages
item.description:
Manage OTA firmware packages. Admin-only. Upload artifacts, list packages, and check processing status.

**Auth:** `admin_token` (must be in Cognito `admin` group).

query.description: Filter by status: ACTIVE or PENDING
List all versions of a specific package (optional)

request.description:
Returns all OTA packages.

**Auth:** Any authenticated user (admin or non-admin token).

**Query params:**
- `status` — filter by status (`ACTIVE`, `SUPERSEDED`, `RECALLED`, `PENDING`, `CORRUPTED`, `DELETED`). Omit or leave empty to return **all statuses**.
- `deviceType` — filter by device type (returns all versions of that package name).

Poll this endpoint after uploading a package until `status` changes from `PENDING` → `ACTIVE` (usually under 5 seconds).

Initiates a firmware upload. Returns either a single presigned S3 URL (SINGLE mode) or per-chunk presigned URLs (MULTIPART mode).

**Upload mode is selected automatically based on `totalSize`:**
- `totalSize` not provided or ≤ 10MB → **SINGLE**: use `uploadUrl` to PUT binary directly
- `totalSize` > 10MB → **MULTIPART**: PUT each `chunkUrls[n].url` with its chunk, then call `POST /upload-artefact/complete`

**Required fields:** `deviceType`, `version`, `releaseType`, `checksum`

**Optional fields:** `totalSize` (bytes), `fileName`, `releaseNotes`

After upload, poll `GET /packages/{{package_name}}/{{package_version}}` until `status=ACTIVE`.

response.name: 200 OK — Upload URL issued
response.body:
{
  "uploadUrl": "https://digilux-ota-artifacts.s3.amazonaws.com/Network_controller_firmware/Network_controller_firmware/4.0.0/HomeAssistantUtility-4.0.0.jar?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=...",
  "s3Key": "Network_controller_firmware/Network_controller_firmware/4.0.0/HomeAssistantUtility-4.0.0.jar",
  "expiresIn": 3600,
  "packageName": "HomeAssistantUtility",
  "version": "4.0.0",
  "deviceType": "Network_controller_firmware",
  "releaseType": "PROD",
  "status": "PENDING",
  "instructions": "PUT binary to uploadUrl with headers: Content-Type: application/octet-stream AND x-amz-meta-upload-token: <uploadToken>. Then poll GET /packages/{packageName}/{version} until status=ACTIVE."
}

response.name: 409 Conflict — Version already ACTIVE

header.description: Required — must match token from Get Upload URL response

request.description:
Step 2 of the upload flow. PUT the binary artifact directly to S3 using the pre-signed URL from the previous step.

- **No Authorization header** — the pre-signed URL handles authentication
- Set `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`
- Select your binary file in Body > file tab
- S3 returns HTTP 200 with an empty body on success

After this completes, poll `List Packages` (with `packageName` filter) to confirm `status` moves to `ACTIVE`. The artifact processor Lambda runs SHA-256 + ECDSA signing automatically.

**Step 2 of MULTIPART upload only.** Call after all chunks have been PUT to S3.

Collect the `ETag` header from each chunk PUT response and include them here.

On success, S3 assembles the file and `artifact_processor` promotes it to `ACTIVE` within seconds. Poll `GET /packages/{{package_name}}/{{package_version}}` for status.

Not needed for SINGLE uploads.

Returns the current status of a specific package version.

**Poll this after upload until `status` is `ACTIVE` or `CORRUPTED`.**

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `PENDING` | Upload in progress or artifact_processor running |
| `ACTIVE` | Upload complete, verified, ready for deployment |
| `CORRUPTED` | Checksum mismatch or token validation failed — re-upload required |

Response includes `sha256`, `artifactSize` once ACTIVE.

Publish (or withdraw) a firmware package so it is visible to end-user devices.

`activated: true`  → package appears in user update checks (must be `status=ACTIVE` first)
`activated: false` → withdraw / pull back the package

**Path params:**
- `packageName` — e.g. `HomeAssistantUtility`
- `version`     — e.g. `1.2.3`

The package must be `status=ACTIVE` (set automatically by the artifact_processor Lambda after upload).

Permanently deletes a package and its S3 artifact.

**Validations (in order):**
1. Package must NOT be `ACTIVE` → `409`
2. `reason` is required → `400`
3. No active deployments (QUEUED / IN_PROGRESS) → `409`
4. SUPERSEDED < 7 days → `409` with `coolingOff: true` (set `force: true` to override)
5. S3 artifact deleted
6. `RECALLED` → soft delete (record stays, `status=DELETED`); others → hard delete

**Body:**
- `reason` (required) — audit log entry
- `force` (optional, default `false`) — override 7-day cooling-off for SUPERSEDED packages

**Cooling-off 409 response:**
```json
{
  "coolingOff": true,
  "supersededDaysAgo": 2.3,
  "coolingOffDays": 7,
  "error": "...was superseded 2.3 day(s) ago..."
}
```

item.name: Device (Admin)
item.description:
Admin endpoint to check what's installed on a specific device and what updates are available.

**Auth:** `admin_token` (must be in Cognito `admin` group).

request.description:
Returns the installed version and available updates for a specific device. Admin-only — no ownership check.

- `deviceId` is the UUID from `digilux_device_data`
- `globalInstalledVersion` — flat version string set by the OTA agent on registration
- `package` — object with `name` (package identifier) and `installedVersion` (package-type-specific version)
- `pendingJobId` is non-null if an active deployment is in progress
- Version comparison uses semver integer tuples — `4.10.0 > 4.2.0`

**404** is returned if the OTA agent has never run on this device.

response.name: 404 Not Found — Device not in OTA inventory

item.name: Deployments
item.description:
Create and manage OTA deployments. A deployment pushes a specific package version to a device or device group via AWS IoT Jobs.

**Auth:** `admin_token` (must be in Cognito `admin` group).

request.description:
Creates an AWS IoT Job to push a package version to a device or device group.

The `job_id` collection variable is auto-populated by the test script.

**targetType values:**
- `THING` — single device; `targetId` = device UUID
- `THING_GROUP` — device group; `targetId` = group name (e.g. `DGX-Canary`)

**rolloutStage values:**
- `CANARY` — max 2 devices/min, first 5 devices
- `BETA` — exponential from 2/min, ~10% of fleet
- `PRODUCTION` — exponential from 5/min, full fleet (default)

**Auto-abort criteria (fleet deployments):**
- >10% of devices FAILED
- >20% of devices TIMEOUT

**Errors:**
- 400 if package is not ACTIVE or device already has this version
- 404 if package or device not found in OTA inventory

response.name: 400 Bad Request — Already installed
400 Bad Request — Package not ACTIVE

request.description: Returns all deployments ordered newest-first. Maximum `limit` is 100.

exec: pm.test('Job reached terminal state: ' + status, () => pm.expect(terminal).to.include(status));
console.log('Job still in progress — re-run to poll');

request.description:
Returns full status of a deployment including per-device progress.

**Job status values:**
- `QUEUED` — created, device not yet acknowledged
- `IN_PROGRESS` — device is downloading/installing
- `SUCCEEDED` — installed and health check passed
- `FAILED` — failed; see `deviceStatuses[id].statusDetail`
- `CANCELLED` — aborted by admin
- `REJECTED` — device rejected the job (precondition not met)

**NEEDS_RECOVERY** in `statusDetail` means both install AND rollback failed. Device requires manual intervention (SSH access).

response.name: 200 OK — NEEDS_RECOVERY (critical — manual intervention required)

request.description:
Cancels the IoT Job for all devices not yet in a terminal state.

**Behaviour:** `force=false` (default) — devices already downloading or installing are NOT interrupted. Only `QUEUED` executions are cancelled.

Devices already in a terminal state (SUCCEEDED, FAILED) are unaffected.
Lists all enrolled beta users. Email is resolved live from Cognito — not stored in DynamoDB. `thingName` is not stored; it is looked up from `digilux_device_data` at deployment time.

Enrolls a user as a beta tester by email.

**Resolution chain:**
1. Cognito `AdminGetUser` by email → `userId`
2. `digilux_device_data` query via `userId-index` GSI → `deviceId` (confirms device exists)
3. Writes `{ userId, deviceId, addedAt, addedBy }` to `digilux_ota_beta_users`

Email and thingName are **not stored**.

The `beta_user_id` collection variable is auto-set by the test script.

**Errors:**
- `400` — email missing
- `404` — email not found in Cognito
- `404` — no device registered for that user
- `409` — user already enrolled

response.name: 404 Not Found — No device

request.description:
Removes a user from the beta program by Cognito `userId` (UUID from `GET /beta-users` response).

Use the `{{beta_user_id}}` variable set by the Add Beta User request, or paste the `userId` directly.

response.name: 404 Not Found

request.description:
Creates a BETA deployment targeting specific enrolled beta devices.

`targetIds` — array of device UUIDs from the `GET /beta-users` response (`deviceId` field).

`thingName` is resolved fresh from `digilux_device_data` at deployment time — not from the beta users table.

Creates a single IoT Job targeting all specified devices as a `THING_LIST`. Max rate: 2 devices/min.

item.name: Full Deployment Flow (Admin)
item.description:
End-to-end admin flow: upload package → wait for ACTIVE → deploy → poll until done.

Run these requests in order. Variables are auto-populated by test scripts.

**Auth:** `admin_token`

request.description:
Request a pre-signed S3 upload URL for a new firmware package.

**Required fields:**
| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| `deviceType` | One of the 4 supported device types | `Network_controller_firmware` |
| `version` | Semantic version string | `1.2.3` |
| `releaseType` | `PROD` (all devices) or `UAT` (canary group only) | `PROD` |

**Supported `deviceType` values:**
| deviceType | Derived filename | operationType |
|---|---|---|
| `Network_controller_firmware` | `HomeAssistantUtility-{version}.jar` | 1 |
| `Network_controller_zigbee_firmware` | `ZigbeeFirmware-{version}.tar` | 2 |
| `Network_controller_Z2M_Firmware` | `Z2MFirmware-{version}.bin` | 3 |
| `Network_controller_Miscellaneous` | `NetControllerMisc-{version}.py` | 4 |
| `Network_controller_zigbee_stack_firmware` | `ZigbeeStackFirmware-{version}.bin` | 5 |

**S3 key format:** `Network_controller_firmware/{deviceType}/{version}/{fileName}`

**Response:** `uploadUrl` (PUT to this), `s3Key`, `packageName`, `status=PENDING`

**Next step:** PUT the binary to `uploadUrl` → artifact_processor promotes to `ACTIVE` automatically.

header.description: Required — must match token from Get Upload URL response

request.description: PUT binary to the pre-signed S3 URL. No Authorization header needed.

exec: console.log('Package not found yet — re-run in a few seconds');

request.description: Poll this endpoint after the S3 upload until `status` becomes `ACTIVE` or `CORRUPTED`. Typically takes 1–5 seconds for artifact_processor to run.
Verify the device shows the new version as an available update before deploying.

exec: console.log('Still in progress — re-run to poll again');

request.description: Re-run every 10–15 seconds until status reaches a terminal state.

item.name: End User Updates
item.description:
User-initiated OTA update flow for the Flutter (homeowner) app.

**Auth:** `user_token` — regular Cognito user, NO admin group required.

**Two available flows:**

1. **Consent Flow** — Creates an IoT Job; device polls AWS IoT for the job and downloads via HTTPS. Best for reliable, trackable updates.
   - Check → Consent → Poll Status

2. **App-Mediated Flow** — No IoT Job; Lambda returns the download URL to the app AND publishes it to the device over MQTT simultaneously. Lighter weight.
   - Check → Get Download Link

**Security:** Users can only see and update devices they own (verified via `digilux_device_data` `userId-index` GSI).

exec: console.log('Devices with updates:', res.devices.filter(d => d.availableVersion).length, '| Total devices:', res.devices.length);

request.description:
Returns all controller devices owned by the calling user and any available updates for each.

- Ownership determined by `userId` (`sub` claim) in the Cognito JWT
- Only devices in `digilux_device_data` under this `userId` are returned
- `otaStatus: NOT_REGISTERED` — device has never run the OTA agent
- Version comparison uses semver integer tuples — `4.10.0 > 4.2.0`
- `pendingJobId` non-null means an update is already in progress

Records the user's explicit consent and triggers the OTA update on their device via an AWS IoT Job.

**Server-side security checks (in order):**
1. Valid Cognito JWT with `sub` claim
2. `deviceId` UUID format validation
3. Device ownership — must be registered under this `userId` in `digilux_device_data`
4. Package must exist and be `ACTIVE`
5. Requested version must be strictly newer than the installed version
6. No update already in progress (`pendingJobId` must be null)
7. Rate limit — max 1 consent per device per 5 minutes

On success, an AWS IoT Job is created and the device downloads the binary via HTTPS from S3.

`job_id` and `consent_id` are auto-saved by the test script.

response.name: 202 Accepted — Update queued
response.body:

  "consentId": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",

409 Conflict — Update already in progress
409 Conflict — Version already installed
409 Conflict — Version not newer than installed
429 Too Many Requests — Rate limited (5 min cooldown)

exec: console.log('Still in progress — re-run to poll again');

request.description:
Returns the current status of a user-initiated (consent) update.

**Security:** The `jobId` must belong to a consent record owned by the calling user. Users cannot query other users' job statuses — 404 is returned if not found or not owned.

**Status values:**
- `QUEUED` — device not yet acknowledged
- `IN_PROGRESS` — downloading/installing (check `progress` %)
- `SUCCEEDED` — installed successfully
- `FAILED` — failed; device may have rolled back automatically
- `CANCELLED` — cancelled by admin
- `REJECTED` — device rejected the job

response.body:

request.description:
Returns a pre-signed S3 download URL for the firmware package AND simultaneously publishes the download payload to the device's OTA MQTT topic (`iot/device/{deviceId}/ota`).

The device receives the URL over MQTT and begins downloading from S3 immediately. The Flutter app also receives the URL and can pass it directly to the device if needed (e.g., if the device was offline when MQTT was published).

**No IoT Job is created** — lighter weight than the consent flow with no 60-minute job timeout.

**MQTT payload sent to device:**
```json
{
  "operationType": 1,
  "packageName": "controller-app",
  "version": "4.0.0",
  "packageType": "deb",
  "downloadUrl": "<S3 pre-signed URL>",
  "sha256": "<hex digest>",
  "signature": "<ECDSA P-256 base64>",
  "size": 12456789,
  "expiresAt": "2026-08-04T15:00:00Z",
  "initiatedBy": "USER_APP",
  "rollback": true
}
```

**Response fields:**
- `downloadUrl` — pre-signed S3 GET URL (1-hour TTL)
- `sha256` — artifact SHA-256 hex digest
- `signature` — ECDSA P-256 signature for authenticity
- `size` — artifact size in bytes
- `expiresAt` — ISO-8601 URL expiry time
- `mqttDelivered` — `true` if device notified; `false` if device offline
- `message` — human-readable status

**Security checks (same as consent, minus rate limit and IoT Job):**
1. Valid JWT with `sub` claim
2. UUID format validation for `deviceId`
3. Device ownership verification
4. Package must be `ACTIVE`
5. Device must be in OTA inventory
6. Version must be strictly newer than installed
7. No pending update in progress

response.name: 200 OK — MQTT delivered (device online)
response.body:
{
  "downloadUrl": "https://digilux-ota-artifacts.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/packages/controller-app/4.0.0/controller-app-4.0.0.deb?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=...",
  "sha256": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855",
  "signature": "MEUCIQDxYqf9zNk3...",
  "packageName": "controller-app",
  "version": "4.0.0",
  "size": 12456789,
  "packageType": "deb",
  "expiresAt": "2026-08-04T15:00:00Z",
  "mqttDelivered": true,
  "message": "Download URL sent to device via MQTT. Device will begin download shortly."
}

response.name: 200 OK — MQTT not delivered (device offline)
response.body:
{
  "downloadUrl": "https://digilux-ota-artifacts.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/packages/controller-app/4.0.0/controller-app-4.0.0.deb?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=...",

item.name: Consent Flow (3 steps)
item.description:
IoT Job-based update flow. Run in order — variables auto-populate.

Best for: trackable, reliable updates with built-in retry and status polling.

exec: console.log('Devices with updates:', res.devices.filter(d => d.availableVersion).length, '| Total devices:', res.devices.length);

request.description: Re-run every 10–15 seconds until status reaches a terminal state.

item.name: App-Mediated Flow (2 steps)
item.description:
MQTT-based update flow. No IoT Job — Lambda publishes the download URL directly to the device over MQTT.

Best for: immediate delivery when the device is online, lower overhead than the consent flow.

exec: console.log('Devices with updates:', res.devices.filter(d => d.availableVersion).length, '| Total devices:', res.devices.length);

request.description: Lambda returns the URL to the app AND publishes it to the device's MQTT topic simultaneously. Check `mqttDelivered` in the response to confirm device was notified.

exec: // Warn if tokens are missing — run '0. Get Tokens' first
try { var p = JSON.parse(atob(jwt.split('.')[1])); return Date.now()/1000 >= p.exp - 60; }
if (!t || isExpired(t)) { console.warn('admin_token missing or expired — run 0. Get Tokens first'); }
